Subject: SOC2 evidence request — network separation for Dedicated/Private

Hi Rachel,

Thanks for agreeing to support Acme's SOC2 readiness review. As part of the control validation (CC6/Logical and physical access; and the infrastructure segmentation narrative) we need a concise packet covering:

- An up-to-date network diagram that annotates Dedicated vs Private deployment boundaries and control-plane vs data-plane paths.
- A short narrative (1-2 pages) describing how the control plane is segregated for Private deployments and where fallbacks occur (model variant routing, cross-region).
- A segregation matrix mapping customer tenancy to network zones and control enforcement points.
- Any proof points or logs demonstrating that control-plane API traffic is isolated from tenant data paths (synthetic request trace or log excerpts are fine; redact PII).

Target timeline: please provide initial evidence by EOD Monday (Nov 2). If a call helps, we can schedule a 30-minute walkthrough.

Attached: Acme intake checklist (for reference).

Appreciate it —
Sarah Liu
Senior Auditor, Vertisys Audit Services

On Sun, Oct 31, 2026 at 10:03 AM Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Sarah —
>
> Thanks for the clear list. Looping in Kimberly (network diagrams/visuals), Karthik (SOC2 lead / control narrative), and Jonas (segmentation matrix). We'll aim to assemble a single packet with the items you requested by EOD Mon Nov 2.

Thanks — quick update from infra: we've updated the diagrams to reflect the recent control-plane split in the Oct release. The new diagram highlights:

- Control plane (API management, rollout service, telemetry collectors) runs in a separate VPC and is reachable only from management subnets and selected site-to-site tunnels for Dedicated customers.
- Private deployments (customer VPC peering or private connect) have a customer-controlled ingress; control-plane outbound calls are sourced from managed NATs in the control VPC.
- Data-plane inference hosts are in tenant-isolated subnets with strict egress ACLs; we use prefix lists to prevent accidental routing back into control-plane management interfaces.
- Fallback routing: when Dedicated capacity is constrained, requests are routed to a shared-hosting pool but only to pre-approved model variants and with KV-cache isolation per tenant. The fallback path is annotated on the diagram.

Attachments in the packet (we will attach to Rachel's outbound):
- network_v4_diagram.png (image/png) — annotated; includes legend for control vs data paths
- segregation_matrix_v2.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet) — service-to-zone mappings
- controlplane-separation-20261031.pdf (application/pdf) — 2-page narrative + sequence diagram for a management API call

Log excerpt: Ops has sanitized a short trace showing a management API session originating from the control VPC, traversing management gateway, and terminating on the host-level agent. We'll redact hostnames and customer identifiers — leaving flow metadata intact.

If Vertisys wants, I'm available Nov 2 1:00–3:00pm PT for a walkthrough.

—Kimberly Park
Senior Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
